links.claim: Conditional finish costs more than a Payment. The XRPL fee formula scales as base_fee × (33 + fulfillment_bytes / 16) before multisign/load effects. Live create/cancel each cost 12 drops. A cancelled 60,000-drop principal is fully returned; its buyer still pays 24 drops in fees. - Synthetic corpus and extractive fixture answers in the proof are labelled; Testnet value transfer is real Testnet execution, with no real value.

Replacement expertise uses a new intent and escrow; gross budget authorization is not replenished by the refund. Each purchase keeps an identity that distinguishes its writer, article version and authorized purpose.

An envelope that cannot authenticate/decrypt, or lacks a failed passage claim, cannot support the passage challenge and remains quarantined and charged. Unsupported escrow writers remain skipped with no exact-payment fallback. Caller hire funding, royalties, change and refunds remain explicit Payments; they are transfers rather than purchases of encrypted article delivery. Offline demonstrations use labelled simulated transactions.

A refund after successful key publication is a separate writer-signed Payment. The ledger does not decide whether prose is useful, truthful or worth its price. A signed passage promise and a verifiable fraud proof establish responsibility for a broken commitment, but a real writer could refuse a refund. The fixture writer cooperates in our demonstrations. This limitation belongs beside the transaction evidence so that a reader does not mistake a cooperative recovery for unilateral buyer protection.

sources.title: What does EscrowCreate do on XRPL?
sources.body:
According to XRPL documentation, EscrowCreate locks funds for a specified recipient until the configured time or cryptographic conditions permit release. [1]

FinishAfter and CancelAfter use ledger time, and a Condition can require a matching fulfillment. Trust-line token escrow requires the issuer's AllowTrustLineLocking permission; MPT escrow has its own capability flags. Holding a token balance alone does not establish escrow eligibility. Creation locks principal but does not pay the recipient. [1]

The EscrowCreate reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using EscrowCreate, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.

sources.title: What does EscrowCancel do on XRPL?
sources.body:
According to XRPL documentation, EscrowCancel returns expired escrowed principal to the sender after the ledger's cancellation deadline. [1]

Passing CancelAfter makes cancellation possible; it does not automatically move money. Any account may submit the cancellation, identifying the original Owner and OfferSequence. An escrow without CancelAfter cannot be canceled this way. Transaction fees remain spent even when the full principal returns to its original owner. [1]

The EscrowCancel reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields.
